verdicts.reason: I opened all four frames myself and every visual detail is exactly as stated. _t0435s: green 19/20, blue 26/26, third bar ~42% WHITE fill on a brown track, yellow '150% DAMAGE' below, NO caption, screen flashed red. _t0430s: 20/20, 26/26, thin white sliver at the left end of the third bar, NO caption. duel_dense 429.0: same fight, third bar EMPTY, 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' printed ON the bar in light grey. _t0425s: overworld, NO third bar at all, the slot prints 'HEAVY STANCE', no banner. Same video id Nr4fQstqHDM, timestamps 425 -> 429.0 -> 430 -> 435. THE FRAME WINS: a caption present at 429.0 and gone at 430 and 435 inside one battle cannot be a hard lock. The code I opened matches the film precisely - §1t113s0§.as:328 'var _loc3_:Number = (param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48);', :336-342 show the caption at ratio==0, :344-347 hide it while 0<ratio<1, and :111 sets that caption to "<font color='#BBBBBB'>" + getString(960) + '</font>' - light grey, which is exactly the grey I see at 429.0. Both fall. Severity is the impact on the ledger, not a defect. ONE honest caveat the finding does not raise: getString(960) has NO entry in the v0.682 string table (I checked strings.json - numeric ids run 0-9010 with 1893 present and nothing between 940 and 980), so the caption TEXT is knowable only from the frame - which is the whole point of the standing invariant.

new_findings.text: The Focus/reload meter has a hard maximum and the HUD does NOT draw it from zero. §1t99s0§.as:249 'this.§1t4415s0§ = 8 * 24;' is the ONLY write to maxFocus anywhere in the 5,162-line player class (grep '§1t4415s0§ *=' returns exactly one line), so FOCUS_MAX = 192 in web v0.717. Android MCSPlayer.as:239 'this.maxreload = 5 * 24;' = 120 - a 60% difference, so anyone porting the meter from the android blobs gets the wrong scale and every derived ratio wrong with it. Second half, and it is the part a recreation will get wrong silently: the HUD bar is NOT focus/maxFocus. §1t113s0§.as:328 'var _loc3_:Number = (param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48);' clamped at :329-332 to a floor of 0 - the visible bar's zero point is 48, its span is 144, and displayed fill f maps to focus = 48 + 144f. The android twin uses a different offset (MCSPlayer.as:1163 'this.tempreload = this.reload - 24;'). This is why the bar reads EMPTY at exactly the focus level where a stance switch becomes affordable, and it closes the 'max' third of RR:195 blocker (3) 'Focus numerics (max/fill/switch-cost)' with a measured number instead of a Ruffle session.
new_findings.build: web v0.717 (android v0.682 = 120 / offset 24 - do not port)
new_findings.lane_impact: L2 skills-meters blocker (3) and L8 ui-hud. FOCUS_MAX = 192 [CONTRACT, web v0.717]. FOCUS_BAR_ZERO = 48, FOCUS_BAR_SPAN = 144 - the HUD widget must subtract 48 from both operands or the bar will read non-empty exactly when the game shows it empty and prints the stance-lock caption.

new_findings.text: The single TextField sitting on the Focus bar is a THREE-STATE readout, and the ledger has it as a one-state lock. §1t113s0§.as:336-343: at ratio == 0 it shows §1t5204s0§, set at :111 to "<font color='#BBBBBB'>" + getString(960) + '</font>' - light grey, and the frame at duel_dense 429.0 shows that grey text reading 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE'. At :344-347, while 0 < ratio < 1, the field is HIDDEN. At :348-358, at ratio >= 1, it switches to §1t5203s0§, set at :110 to "<font color='#000000'>" + getString(175) + '</font>' - black - and strings.json['175'] resolves getString(175) to 'Critical Hit', with :352 firing §1t1516s0§('Snd_criticalDamage') exactly once on the transition into that state. So the game's own HUD names the full meter a CRIT state, which is independent corroboration that the full-meter branch at §1t99s0§.as:3272 is the crit and not something else. NOTE THE STRING-TABLE HOLE, stated plainly: getString(960) has NO entry in the v0.682 table (strings.json numeric ids run 0-9010, 1893 present, nothing between 940 and 980), so the empty-state caption TEXT is recoverable ONLY from a frame. The measurement docs and the code both fail here and the film does not.

new_findings.text: The three per-stance full-Focus evade passives are keyed on skill ids 1074, 1075 and 1076 (§1t120s0§.as:108/:110/:112, 'public static var ...:int = 1074/1075/1076'), and THOSE IDS ARE NOT IN skilldata.xml. I checked the table directly: reference/extracted/skilldata.xml carries ids 1000-1073 plus 1500 and 1501; grep '<id>107[0-9]</id>' returns 1070,1071,1072,1073 and stops. resolved_names.json['skilldata.xml']['resolved'] likewise ends at 1073. Two consequences the corpus has nowhere. (1) The 75-skill table is the ANDROID v0.682 skill set (C2: those four XMLs are android-sourced), and web v0.717 references at least three skills it does not contain - so '75 skills' is a v0.682 count, not a v0.717 count, and the skill roster has an unmeasured build delta. (2) The names and descriptions of 1074-1076 are UNRESOLVABLE from any extracted table; the only artifact that names them is film - the skill card at reference/frames/zFtCaTO0_1M/seg-03/frames/frame_0013.jpg reads '(PASSIVE SKILL) / ALLOWS YOU TO EVADE ATTACKS WHILE SLASHING IN THIS STANCE WHEN YOUR FOCUS BAR IS FULL.' This is a clean instance of the standing invariant: the payload table and the frame disagree about what skills exist, and THE FRAME WINS.
new_findings.build: web v0.717 vs android v0.682 — a real roster divergence
new_findings.lane_impact: L2 skills-meters: the 75-skill roster must be labelled v0.682. At least three v0.717 skills (1074/1075/1076) sit outside it with no row, no chi cost and no cooldown recoverable from any table — a hole the '75 skills' count currently hides.

new_findings.text: The build-parity trap this packet flags for CRIT_MULT is not a one-off; the android damage and reach tuning diverges from web across the board, so the android blobs are unsafe as a source for ANY combat number. Reading the two twins side by side: DAMAGE - web §1t99s0§.as:3262 Light '_loc1_ * (0.5 + 0.4 * mastery * 0.1)' vs android MCSPlayer.as:3205 'baseDamage * (0.5 + 0.5 * lightMastery * 0.01)'; web :3265 Balanced '(1 + 0.2 * mastery * 0.1)' vs android :3208 '(1 + 0.5 * balancedMastery * 0.01)'; web :3270 Heavy '_loc1_ * 1.4' vs android :3213 'baseDamage * 1.5'. REACH - web :3094 Light 'this.§1t4420s0§ * 1.4' vs android :3030 'this.baseSlashLength * 1.5'; web :3105 Balanced '(1 + 0.2 * mastery * 0.1)' vs android :3041 '(1 + 0.5 * balancedMastery * 0.01)'. METER - web max 192 vs android 120; web stance-switch cost a flat 48 vs android proportional (maxreload/3 or -maxreload/6). Every one of these is a number a ledger row could be built on. The mastery terms are not even the same shape: web multiplies mastery by 0.1, android by 0.01, so the two builds' mastery curves are on different scales and a value 'confirmed' in one is meaningless in the other.
new_findings.build: both — the point IS the divergence
new_findings.quote: web §1t99s0§.as:3270 '_loc2_ = _loc1_ * 1.4;' ‖ android MCSPlayer.as:3213 'maxDamage = baseDamage * 1.5;' ‖ web :3094 'this.§1t4417s0§ = this.§1t4420s0§ * 1.4;' ‖ android :3030 'this.slashLength = this.baseSlashLength * 1.5;'
new_findings.ledger_text: 3. **The stance tables (dmg 0.9/1.2/1.4, reach 300/200/100) are MASTERY-9 CEILING values, not base.**
new_findings.lane_impact: Lane-wide. Every combat row sourced from an android blob needs a WEB re-read before it can be graded CONTRACT, and the C2 caveat should be widened from 'the four data XMLs' to 'all android-sourced combat tuning'. Concretely: Heavy is x1.4 in web and x1.5 in android on BOTH damage and (for Light) reach, and the mastery coefficient differs by a factor of 10 in shape.

new_findings.text: The dan titles do not depend on the v0.682 string table at all, because the WEB build hardcodes the ladder twice - once by string id and once in plain ASCII. §1t408s0§.as:532-566 switches on the same dan value and writes literals: case 0 '' · 1 '(nidan)' · 2 '(sandan)' · 3 '(yondan)' · 4 '(godan)' · 5 '(rokudan)' · 6 '(nanadan)' · 7 '(hachidan)' · 8 '(kyudan)' · 9 and default '(judan)', each of dan 3-5 appending getString(465), dan 6-7 getString(466), dan 8-9 and default getString(467). Set that beside §1t5957s0§.as:3063-3102, which for the same cases writes getString(456)..getString(464) resolving in strings.json to (弐段)(参段)(四段)(五段)(六段)(七段)(八段)(九段)(十段): nidan=弐段, sandan=参段, ... judan=十段, and the SAME shogo boundaries. Two independent web-side renderings agreeing rank-for-rank is a direct discharge of the S0-3 UI-copy caveat FOR THIS ROW, and it also re-proves from the web build alone that displayed dan = STAT_DAN + 1 (state 1 prints 'nidan', the second dan). It further kills the wiki 'dan rank 5 (kyudan)' garble that RR:164-165 rests on: kyudan is STAT_DAN 8, not 5.

new_findings.ledger_text: 7. **`MAX_DAN_RANK=10` and `tenthGold=100` should be INFERRED, not CONTRACT.** The only wiki datum is garbled ("dan rank 5 (kyudan)" — kyudan=9th)

new_findings.text: A pointer defect in the banked ledger that will misroute the next lane. LEDGER_EVIDENCE.md:1510 closes with 'the crit PROC rule (RR:159 blocker (5)) is still open'. Blocker (5) is not at RR:159. REBUILD_READINESS.md:158-160 is the stance-lock item (item 4 of the corrections list) and carries no blockers; the 'crit **proc** rule (chance vs deterministic) - entirely absent' text is blocker (5) of the skills-meters ledger at REBUILD_READINESS.md:195. I verified both lines directly. The consequence is not cosmetic: a critic grepping 'RR:159' to see whether the stance-lock row has been touched gets a hit that is actually about crit, and a critic grepping for prior work on the proc rule at RR:195 gets zero. That is exactly the failure mode that let the NF-S27D-3 author assert "'RR:159' returns zero hits" - the string is there, attached to the wrong subject.

new_findings.text: LEAD, not a close. RR:165 says 'film shows a **flat +25 gold** every rebirth, no 10th-rebirth tier'. The android rebirth routine does have a tier: StatsManager.as:2201-2207, immediately before the dan increment, reads 'if(getPlayerStats(STAT_DAN) == 8) { changeStat(STAT_HGOLD,20); } else { changeStat(STAT_HGOLD,5); }'. That is +5 on every rebirth and +20 on the one that takes you to dan 9. I am NOT claiming this refutes RR:165, and I did not find a web-side twin in the time I had: STAT_HGOLD is a distinct stat from the coin currency the film shows, and I have no artifact tying the two together, so under §0 the honest answer on the identification is STILL_UNHELD. What IS held is that the android rebirth path contains a dan-8 special case, which is precisely the shape of thing RR:165 asserts does not exist. Whoever rewrites RR:164-165 must resolve STAT_HGOLD against the on-screen currency before grading either way.
